name: Peru Organic Finca La Esperanza G1, San Martin
origin: Peru, San Martin, Soritor (Finca La Esperanza, Walter Gutierrez)
vendor_notes: Chocolate and cherry, toasty, nutty, sweet aroma. Citrus, malt, pine and semi-sweet chocolate; low acidity, full body, well balanced. Brightness 4/7, body 5/7, sweetness 6/7, balance 6/7. Grown 900-2,000 m. Organic, FT, RA.
goal: Medium roast: chocolate, malt and sweetness with full body
rationale: A washed mix of Caturra, Typica and Catimor from a wide 900-2,000 m range, so bean density and size vary: a moderate charge (188 C) and a long Maillard (about 3:30 of it) help it develop evenly instead of tipping the small beans. Its strengths are chocolate, malt and body, not acidity, so it is taken to a medium roast: DTR ~22% and ~15 C after first crack. Burner steps start ~2 min before FC because RoR on this roaster lags burner changes by 45-60 s. FC 188 C is from the Honduras on this probe.
steps: Preheat to 188 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 188. Burner 72%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:36 near 108 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 178 C (~6:17): burner 46%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:15 at ~188 C: burner 42%, air 55. Then 38%.
Drop ~9:20 at ~203 C (15 C after FC).

rest.note: Medium roast degasses faster than a light one. Chocolate and malt are fullest around a week; past ~2.5 weeks it flattens.

history.note: Initial medium-roast plan for a friend, from the Coffee Bean Corral page and calibration from the 2026-09-29 roasts (TP ~0:40, Honduras FC 188.9 C).

Re-fitted the first 3-4 minutes to five real roasts (2026-09-29 to 10-02): on this roaster TP comes at ~0:35 at 108-116 C (not ~0:42 at ~100 C), RoR is highest right after TP and only falls, dry end lands ~3:35-3:55 and FC ~7:12-7:25 at 187-189 C. Earlier versions put the start 10-20 C too low, which invited cutting heat early and a hot finish. FC temperature, roast level and development are unchanged.
